findings.title: Error-Based SQL Injection Detected in 'q' (SQLite)
findings.description: Submitting a harmless delimiter probe on parameter 'q' resulted in an unhandled SQLite database syntax error leaked directly in the HTTP response.
findings.evidence: DBMS Detected: SQLite | Error snippet: "sqlite3.OperationalError: near \"'\": syntax error" | Confirmatory probe: doubling quote delimiter successfully restored valid SQL syntax.
findings.remediation: Implement parameterized queries (prepared statements) using parameter placeholders (e.g. ?). Disable verbose server error messages and database stack traces in production.
findings.secure_code_example: cursor.execute('SELECT id, name, category, in_stock FROM training_products WHERE name = ?', (user_input,))
findings.verification_steps:
1. Replace query concatenation with parameter binding.
2. Re-run SQLGuard scanner: ensure HTTP 200 is returned with zero SQL exceptions.
3. Verify unit tests with special characters (' " \ ;).

findings.title: Database Query Surface Identified: 'q'
findings.description: The parameter 'q' appears to pass dynamic filtering or search terms to backend storage.
findings.remediation: Ensure this parameter is handled using parameterized SQL queries and strict input type validation.
findings.verification_steps: Ensure unit tests confirm SQL syntax errors cannot be induced through this parameter.

limitations: Assessment was restricted to harmless, non-destructive boundary probes.
Second-order SQL injection and asynchronous database tasks are not assessed in this scope.
WAF rules or network throttling may suppress or alter error disclosures.
remediation_checklist: Migrate all dynamic SQL statements to parameterized queries / prepared statements.
Enforce strict input validation using allowlists for table/column names.
Disable verbose database error display and stack traces in production environments.
Configure database users with least privilege access permissions.
Implement automated CI/CD static security code analysis.
